status: Senate last recorded action 2026-02-24 canceled the February 26 hearing and scheduled a March 5 hearing; final 2026 index lists hearing stage, indicating non-enactment in that session.
key_provisions: First reading proposed interconnection and demand-response rules for large-load customers with monthly demand of at least 25 MW and load factor above 80%, including a 25% capacity contribution with a surplus-interconnection offset, expedited processing for 100% capacity, and priority requiring 100% capacity and prevailing wages.

sponsors: Senators Feldman, Hester, Ferguson, Brooks, Gile, Harris, Kagan, Simonaire, M. Washington, and Watson
status: Senate passed 2026-04-06; House committee reported favorable with amendments 2026-04-13; final 2026 index stops at that report. Chapter 353 is HB1532, not SB0841.
key_provisions: Senate third reader proposed a large-load registry, voluntary clean-capacity rating and interconnection process and a qualified Baltimore City data-center construction restriction; this describes that Senate version, not the later House committee amendments.

status: Senate last recorded action 2026-02-04 scheduled a 2026-02-18 hearing; final 2026 index lists hearing stage, indicating non-enactment in that session.
key_provisions: First reading proposed authority for Baltimore City and counties to establish a qualified-data-center personal-property tax subclass and special rate; the proposed June 1 effective date and application to taxable years beginning after June 30 are not enacted dates.

status: Signed 2026-09-23; effective immediately. Current legal effect unverified.
key_provisions: Establishes a framework and task force for covered data centers, generally facilities at 25 MW or more or meeting the referenced statutory large-load definition, subject to stated exclusions; following specified review triggers, agencies defer substantive review for not-aligned, non-performing, or non-seeking projects until required local approvals, plan consistency, and required water or wastewater authorizations are documented, and limit discretionary incentives and support, to the extent lawful; disclosure and reporting conditions apply prospectively subject to transition protections.
